feedbackActionPlan.summary: Add a broader Joint Pin selection list to the custom cue configurator and provide an Other/write-in path so customers can specify uncommon or proprietary joint types without abandoning the order.
feedbackActionPlan.customerImpact: Customers with common cue joints can choose the right compatibility option faster, while customers with uncommon or uncertain joint pins can still complete checkout and give enough detail for follow-up instead of guessing.
feedbackActionPlan.businessImpact: Reduces pre-sale support friction, prevents incompatible shaft or cue builds caused by missing joint options, and preserves conversion for custom orders that need manual review.
feedbackActionPlan.confidence: High confidence in the product need and recommended option set based on common billiards joint references and ecommerce customization patterns. Confidence is reduced because this checkout appears to contain a billiards physics codebase rather than the live website source, so implementation surfaces are expressed as assumptions.

researchFindings.finding: Raw feedback asks for more choices on joint pin selection and an option for customers to write in the joint type they have.
Repository inspection found no website or ecommerce frontend files; assumption: the live site has a product configurator or ecommerce theme outside this checkout.

Common pool cue joint choices to offer include 5/16 x 14, 5/16 x 18, 3/8 x 10, 3/8 x 11, 3/8 x 14, Uni-Loc Quick Release, Uni-Loc Radial, Mezz Wavy, Viking Quick Release, and a manual Other option. Predator, CueSight, Uni-Loc, and billiards retailer guides list these or closely related joint types as common manufacturer or replacement-shaft compatibility categories.

Joint compatibility is exact: similar-looking pins such as 5/16 x 14 versus 5/16 x 18, 3/8 x 10 versus Radial, or Uni-Loc Quick Release versus standard threaded joints should not be treated as interchangeable.

Shopify-style ecommerce implementations can persist custom selections as line item properties on cart add; the selected joint pin and Other text should travel with the cart, checkout, order admin, confirmation email, and fulfillment paperwork.

implementationPlan.step: Locate the source of truth for custom cue option definitions, especially the existing Joint Pin dropdown values, labels, pricing metadata, and order payload mapping.

Replace the narrow Joint Pin list with a deterministic ordered list: 5/16 x 14, 5/16 x 18, 3/8 x 10, 3/8 x 11, 3/8 x 14, Uni-Loc Quick Release, Uni-Loc Radial, Mezz Wavy, Viking Quick Release, Not sure - contact me, and Other - write in.

Add conditional UI that displays a required text input only when Other - write in is selected. Label it "Joint pin type" and helper text "Enter the exact joint type, cue brand/model, or measurements if known."

Validate the write-in field client-side and server-side: trim whitespace, require 2 to 80 characters, allow letters, numbers, spaces, slash, hyphen, period, plus, parentheses, and apostrophe, reject URLs or markup, and show a clear inline error before add-to-cart.

Normalize saved order data into two explicit fields: Joint Pin Selection for the chosen dropdown value and Joint Pin Write-In for the customer-entered text when applicable. Do not overwrite the dropdown value with free text.

Add fulfillment notes generated from the selection: standard options should show the exact selected pin; Other and Not sure should flag "manual compatibility review required before production" and include the customer text.
Ensure cart summary, checkout attributes or line item properties, order admin, customer confirmation, and production work order all display the joint pin information consistently.
Add a small help affordance near the field explaining that joint pin thread and quick-release systems must match exactly and customers should not guess if unsure.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The Joint Pin selector includes the expanded list of standard and proprietary options plus Not sure - contact me and Other - write in.
Selecting Other - write in reveals a required text field; selecting any other option hides and clears that field.
The order cannot be added to cart when Other - write in is selected and the write-in value is empty, too long, or contains markup or a URL.
Standard joint pin selections are stored and displayed in cart, checkout/order review, order admin, customer confirmation, and fulfillment output.
Other and Not sure orders are clearly marked for manual compatibility review before production or shipment.
Existing orders that use current joint pin values remain readable and map to the new labels without data loss.

risks.risk: Adding too many options can overwhelm customers; mitigate by grouping common standard threads first and proprietary/quick-release options afterward.
Free-text entries can be ambiguous or misspelled; mitigate with helper text, length limits, sanitized input, and a manual review flag.
Some manufacturers have variants within a nominal joint type, especially 3/8 x 10 and proprietary quick-release systems; do not automatically promise compatibility for write-ins.
If ecommerce order templates are not updated, the website may collect the value but fulfillment may not see it.

openQuestions.question: Which ecommerce platform or configurator owns the live Joint Pin field?
Should any new joint pin choices change price, lead time, or available shaft compatibility?
Does fulfillment want Other and Not sure orders held automatically, tagged in admin, or routed to customer service?
Are brand-specific aliases such as Predator Uni-Loc or Mezz Wavy already used internally and should they appear in labels?
